metadata.note: RTD Denver's light rail network (C, D, E, T, W, R lines), as of the GTFS feed pulled from https://nodejs-prod.rtd-denver.com/api/download/gtfs/google_transit.zip. Route geometry, frequency (headway_min, from real scheduled trip counts on a representative Wednesday), and avg_speed_kmh (from real scheduled trip duration) are all sourced directly from the agency's own GTFS feed, same methodology as data/rtd_denver.geojson (RTD's separate commuter rail file) and data/amtrak.geojson. As of this Aug 2026 pull, RTD is in the final phase of its multi-year Downtown Rail Reconstruction Project (service changes effective June 7 2026): the D Line is suspended and rerouted away from Union Station, the H Line is suspended entirely (and so is not in this file), the temporary T Line was created to bridge the Southeast Corridor, and the C Line was reinstated after a 2020-2023 hiatus to keep Union Station access for southwest-corridor riders. Historical segments (pre-2026) were added from RTD's own corridor-opening history (the original 1994 Central Corridor starter line, the 2000/2002 Southwest Corridor and Central Platte Valley extensions, the 2006 T-REX Southeast Corridor, the 2013 West Corridor, the 2017 I-225 Rail Line, and the 2019 Southeast Rail Extension to RidgeGate Parkway), sourced from RTD and local news coverage. Unlike the GTFS-sourced 2026 segment, these older headway numbers are not derived from real historical timetables and should be read as illustrative estimates, not precise data.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
